DRIFT_001.description: New artifact with 600-series or SESSION6** attribution
DRIFT_001.rationale: Unauthorized artifact creation in a dormant lane = governance violation. Matches AGENTS.md §13.5 CRITICAL standard for unauthorized activity.

DRIFT_002.description: Any mandatory gate transitions from FAIL to PASS
DRIFT_002.rationale: Gate transition represents changed conditions meriting investigation, not an emergency requiring halt. Correctly graded HIGH (investigation-triggering), not CRITICAL (emergency). Matches AGENTS.md §13.5 HIGH standard ('Certified denominator mismatch' tier).
DRIFT_002.notable: Action explicitly states 'Do not automatically activate — a gate transition is a review trigger, not an activation trigger.' This is a critical safeguard against accidental activation. Verified against S600 Charter §5.2 which requires all 3 leads to vote.

DRIFT_003.description: S600 Charter file modified without REVISION_HISTORY.md entry
DRIFT_003.rationale: Undocumented charter modification = governance tampering. Matches AGENTS.md §13.5 CRITICAL standard ('Unexpected hash change in any baseline file').

DRIFT_004.description: New REVISION_HISTORY.md entry attributing work to 600-series
DRIFT_004.rationale: Unauthorized claim of 600-series authority without Executive Board vote = governance violation. Severity CRITICAL is appropriate — this would represent bypass of the activation conditions.

DRIFT_005.description: GAP-3 resolution: Governance Board accepts S725 Row 16 ownership
DRIFT_005.rationale: Governance hygiene improvement — not a threat. LOW is appropriate for a positive governance signal.

DRIFT_006.description: 800-series certification completes (100% Certified across all packs)
DRIFT_006.rationale: Major portfolio milestone that triggers AV_4 re-evaluation but does not itself activate 600. Action explicitly states 'Does not automatically trigger activation.' Correctly prevents milestone-creep into activation territory.

drift_signals_review.overlap_with_existing_governance: Minimal and complementary. The S602 DRIFT signals monitor dormant-lane GOVERNANCE state (charter integrity, activation conditions, authority attribution) while AGENTS.md §13.5 drift signals monitor RUNTIME artifact integrity (file hashes, parse-counts, certified counts, FD-045, app.js). Different layers — no functional overlap. DRIFT_003 (charter modified without REVISION_HISTORY entry) conceptually overlaps with AGENTS.md §13.5 'Unexpected hash change' signal but is more precisely scoped to the governance-process dimension (modification without documentation) rather than raw hash change alone.

stewardship_ownership.primary_reviewer_evidence: S725 Ownership Matrix Row 5 (Governance trigger monitoring — primary: Governance Auditor) and Row 7 (T0 protocol execution — primary: Governance Auditor). The Governance Auditor is the OPERATIONAL executor of all cadenced checks. This is distinct from the Governance Board which is the STEWARDSHIP owner per Row 16.
stewardship_ownership.secondary_reviewer_evidence: S725 Row 1 (CURRENT_BASELINES.md maintenance — primary: Baseline Maintainer). Hash verification of the S600 Charter at T0 is correctly assigned to the Baseline Maintainer, whose role encompasses hash integrity across all tracked files.
stewardship_ownership.escalation_evidence: S725 Row 16 (600-series deferred lane stewardship — primary: Governance Board). Escalation goes to the lane's steward. Consistent across all S725 matrix rows (Governance Board is the universal escalation owner).
stewardship_ownership.charter_reference: S600 Charter §5.2 — 'A new Executive Board vote is required... All three leads must vote to activate.' The framework correctly identifies that only the Executive Board (3 leads) can vote on 600-series activation.
stewardship_ownership.acceptance_detail: S725 Row 16 assigns stewardship to Governance Board but acceptance has not occurred (0/6 GAPs accepted per S725 Ownership Matrix §4 verification). S602 Stewardship Alignment Review confirms P1/P2 violations (no orphaned responsibility, ownership transfers require acceptance) are governance-process issues. The Monitoring Framework correctly notes this as pending. All cadenced checks still function — the Governance Auditor executes checks regardless of acceptance status — but formal stewardship authority remains unconfirmed.

operational_feasibility.t0_overhead: 30 seconds claimed — realistic. The 5 checks are all read-only, passive scans on files that are small (S600 Charter: 361 lines, S601 Board Decision: markdown, S725 Ownership: JSON). The heaviest check (C5: Certified count verification) is already part of the standard T0 protocol (AGENTS.md §9, step 3) and would not be re-run for the 600-specific T0 — it is a cross-reference of an already-computed value. Estimated actual time: 20-40 seconds for the 600-specific increment.
operational_feasibility.deep_audit_effort_estimate: 1-2 sessions of governance agent time. 8 comprehensive checks spanning economic modeling, binding constraint analysis, AV_1-AV_5 re-evaluation, portfolio metrics, and cross-series impact. Comparable to a S601-class governance review session. Appropriate for a 20-session cadence.
operational_feasibility.annual_effort_estimate: ~1 session. 6 checks primarily assessing whether charter and portfolio assumptions still hold. Leverages S725/S726/S727 governance infrastructure rather than requiring independent construction. Cadence anchors correctly to S725 Row 16.
operational_feasibility.rapid_pulse_effort_estimate: ~15-30 minutes of agent time. 5 checks, primarily read-only and cross-reference against existing registries. Lightweight enough to execute as a single agent task within a standard session.

gap_analysis.cross_lane_boundary_checking: ADEQUATE. Rapid Pulse (every 5 sessions) includes 'Verify no cross-lane boundary violations (600 artifacts in 300/700/800 spaces)' — frequent enough to catch boundary drift. Deep Audit (every 20 sessions) includes 'Cross-series dependency impact' — comprehensive cross-lane analysis at the strategic level. Both cadences cover the boundary dimension.
gap_analysis.all_clear_reporting_mechanism: MINOR GAP — No explicit artifact for 'all clear, nothing changed.' The framework defines output artifacts only for Deep Audit and Annual reviews (when findings are produced). T0 and Rapid Pulse checks execute silently — no 'T0 600-monitoring PASS' entry is generated. Mitigation: standard session reports (like this S603 activation report) serve as the documentation that checks were performed. The absence of an escalation IS the all-clear. Acceptable for a dormant lane but could be enhanced with a lightweight 'S6XX_T0_600_MONITORING_PASS.json' stamp at each T0.
gap_analysis.drift_signal_completeness: ADEQUATE. 6 signals cover: unauthorized artifacts (DRIFT_001), activation-condition drift (DRIFT_002), charter tampering (DRIFT_003), unauthorized authority claims (DRIFT_004), governance hygiene improvement (DRIFT_005), and portfolio-milestone triggers (DRIFT_006). The signals span the full risk surface: artifact creation, document integrity, authority attribution, condition drift, and milestone-triggered re-evaluation.
gap_analysis.redundancy_with_agents_md_t0_tmid_tend: NONE — complementary. The S602 framework monitors dormant-lane governance (charter integrity, activation conditions, attribution). The AGENTS.md §13 T0-Tmid-Tend sequence monitors active runtime artifacts (pack file hashes, parse counts, certified counts, FD-045, app.js). The two monitoring systems operate at different layers and do not overlap. A 600-series drift signal firing does not trigger the AGENTS.md T0-Tmid-Tend sequence — it triggers the S602-defined escalation path (primarily to the Governance Auditor/Board).
gap_analysis.gap3_blocking_governance: ACKNOWLEDGED — GAP-3 (Governance Board acceptance of S725 Row 16) remains PENDING. This does not prevent the Monitoring Framework from operating: the Governance Auditor executes all checks regardless. However, escalation authority is weakened — if the Governance Board has not formally accepted stewardship, a CRITICAL escalation (DRIFT_001/003/004) may encounter an ownership vacuum at the top. This is a pre-existing governance issue affecting all 6 GAPs, not a framework-specific defect.

conclusion: Monitoring Framework is ACTIVATED. All 4 cadences are viable with defined frequencies, complete checks, documented actions, and appropriate scope. All 6 drift signals are clearly described, correctly severity-assigned per AGENTS.md §13.5 standards, and carry explicit actions with anti-automatic-activation safeguards (DRIFT_002, DRIFT_006 explicitly state 'Do not automatically activate'). Stewardship ownership is correctly assigned — Governance Auditor as operational executor (S725 Rows 5, 7), Baseline Maintainer as hash verifier (S725 Row 1), Governance Board as escalation recipient (S725 Row 16), Executive Board as activation voter (S600 Charter §5.2). Minor gap: no explicit 'all-clear' artifact for T0/Rapid Pulse passes, but standard session reporting mitigates this. GAP-3 acceptance remains pending but does not block monitoring operations.
